back: The maintenance of a constant internal environment within narrow limits.
notes: Example: core body temperature kept close to 37 °C.

back: A change from the set point is detected and responses bring the condition back towards the set point.

front: Skin structures involved in temperature control?
back: Hairs and hair erector muscles, sweat glands, temperature receptors, sensory neurones, blood vessels, fatty tissue.

front: What is the role of the brain in temperature control?
back: It monitors blood temperature, receives impulses from skin receptors and sends impulses to effectors.
Widening of the arterioles supplying the skin capillaries, so more blood flows near the surface and more heat is lost.
Narrowing of the arterioles supplying the skin capillaries, so less blood flows near the surface and less heat is lost.

front: How does sweating cool the body?
back: Water in sweat evaporates from the skin, taking heat from it.

front: How does shivering warm the body?
back: Rapid involuntary muscle contractions increase respiration, which releases heat.

front: Responses when the body is too hot?
back: Vasodilation, more sweating, hairs lie flat.

front: Responses when the body is too cold?
back: Vasoconstriction, shivering, hairs stand up, less sweating.
